LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND NOUNS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, part of Strand 1 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we use compound nouns when communicating?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an audio recording on human rights,

2. identify the compound nouns used in the text,

3. work with peers to categorise compound nouns into two-word or three-word nouns from a given list,

4. form separate and hyphenated compound nouns by combining two or more words,

5. form plurals of compound nouns from a completion table,

6. write sentences using compound nouns in their singular and plural forms,

7. search online and offline for more examples of compound nouns,

8. use compound nouns to form sentences from a substitution table,

9. assess the correctness of the sentences with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio recording on human rights,
2. identify the compound nouns used in the text,
3. work with peers to categorise compound nouns into two-word or three-word nouns from a given list,
4. form separate and hyphenated compound nouns by combining two or more words,
5. form plurals of compound nouns from a completion table,
6. write sentences using compound nouns in their singular and plural forms,
7. search online and offline for more examples of compound nouns,
8. use compound nouns to form sentences from a substitution table,
9. assess the correctness of the sentences with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner work with peers categorise compound nouns

• Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner shows concerted attention to detail when forming separate and hyphenated

compound nouns by combining two or more words.

• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner engages in self- driven tasks while using compound nouns in sentences.

Values:
Respect: It is promoted as the learner displays patience while working with peers to identify the compound nouns in the text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Effective communication: It is boosted as the learner communicates using the newly acquired compound nouns.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the use of compound nouns in learning similar concept in other languages such as Kiswahili.
